title: Nonperturbative Bounds on the Ground-State Energy of Lattice QED
abstract: We establish nonperturbative bounds on the ground-state energy of lattice quantum electrodynamics with naive fermions in Coulomb gauge, within the Gaussian photon approximation. Our central result is a spectral comparison theorem showing that, in the thermodynamic limit, the minimum fermionic energy density over all link configurations coincides with that of the trivial gauge configuration. The proof exploits a logarithmic determinant representation and dimensional reduction, without relying on reflection positivity, and applies to lattices of either parity. Combining this result with the positivity of the electromagnetic and Coulomb Hamiltonians, we derive an explicit lower bound on the interacting ground-state energy. Finite-lattice counterexamples show that the thermodynamic limit is essential.

bite.hook: New nonperturbative bounds prove the ground-state energy of lattice QED is minimized by the trivial gauge configuration.
tldr: The authors established rigorous bounds on the ground-state energy of lattice quantum electrodynamics using the Gaussian photon approximation.
They used a spectral comparison theorem and logarithmic determinant representation to analyze energy densities.
The study proves that the minimum energy density occurs at the trivial gauge configuration in the thermodynamic limit.
bite.whyItMatters: Understanding the ground state of lattice QED is fundamental to high-energy physics; these bounds provide a solid mathematical foundation for complex simulations.
bite.eli5: Think of a landscape with many valleys. This paper proves that for a specific type of quantum field theory, the lowest point (the ground state) is always at the simplest, most 'boring' spot, rather than hidden in a complex, messy configuration.
